newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY 0.5 MLN T SURPLUS SUGAR BEET SEEN EXPORTED.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY 0.5 MLN T SURPLUS SUGAR BEET SEEN EXPORTED.

text.p: Hungary's better than expected sugar beet harvest would probably leave some 500,000 tonnes of root for export after domestic demand has been satisfied, an industry official said on Monday.

"Although the sugar content per beet is relatively low, this is offset by the higher than expected root weight due to almost permanent rains since mid-august," Andras Angeli, Chairman of the Sugar Industry Association told Reuters.
Sugar content at the last test, released on September 27, was 14.1 percent, up from 13.5 percent two weeks earlier but lower than last year's figure of 14.3 percent.
Hungary's domestic sugar demand will be somewhere around 480,000 tonnes, as the state reserves used up during September will have to be replenished again, Angeli said.
Heavy rains, although boosting root weight, have significantly delayed harvesting, he added.

"The delay is somewhere between two to two and a half weeks," he said, adding that this week all sugar factories will gear up to full capacity, as the fields have dried somewhat and if no further rains come, the production should be continuos, Angeli said.
